'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023-present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Twelve-Day War]]
***[[United States strikes on Iranian nuclear sites]]
****A preliminary assessment by the U.S. [[Defense Intelligence Agency]] finds that [[Iran]]'s [[Nuclear program of Iran|nuclear program]] may have only been set back by a few months after the U.S. airstrikes, with the [[Zippe-type centrifuge|centrifuges]] required to [[Enriched uranium|enrich uranium]] left largely intact, contradicting previous claims made by [[U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] that the facilities were "obliterated". [https://apnews.com/article/iran-nuclear-program-military-strikes-trump-f0fc085a2605e7da3e2f47ff9ac0e01d (AP)]
****After U.S. president Donald Trump rejects the DIA assessment as "[[fake news]]", U.S. [[Director of the Central Intelligence Agency|Central Intelligence Agency director]] [[John Ratcliffe]] says that the CIA assesses that several key Iranian nuclear facilities were severely damaged in the airstrikes, likely requiring years to rebuild. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c5yk942y437o (BBC News)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Israel]]i forces kill at least 78 [[Palestinians]] in the [[Gaza Strip]], with at least 14 who were seeking [[humanitarian aid]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/6/25/israeli-attacks-kill-at-least-51-as-trump-signals-progress-in-gaza-talks (Al Jazeera)] 
***Seven Israeli soldiers are killed in [[Khan Yunis]] when an explosive device affixed to their [[Armored Corps (Israel)|armored vehicle]] detonates. [https://apnews.com/article/israel-hamas-war-gaza-06-25-2025-fa3d0a63c2b78a2e95984f1122b89317 (AP)]
*[[Nigerian bandit conflict]]
**At least 17 [[Nigerian Armed Forces|soldiers]] are killed when groups of bandits attack three [[Nigerian Army|Army bases]] in [[Kaduna State|Kaduna]] and [[Niger State]]s in [[Nigeria]]. The Army and [[Nigerian Air Force|Air Force]] reports they have launched counteroffensives against the bandit gangs. [https://www.dw.com/en/soldiers-killed-in-bandit-attacks-on-nigerian-army-bases/a-73041094 (DW)]

'''Business and economy'''
*The first train from [[North Korea]] arrives at the [[Moscow Yaroslavsky railway station|Yaroslavsky railway station]] in [[Moscow]], [[Russia]], after a five-year pause due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. [https://tass.com/economy/1980905 (TASS)]
*[[Online dating]] service [[Bumble]] announces it will [[Layoff|lay off]] 30% of its global workforce, equal to at least 240 jobs. [https://apnews.com/article/bumble-layoffs-cost-cutting-ea412ce53032239ba61d968c86018c8b (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Bangui school stampede]]
**Twenty-nine people are killed and 280 others are injured after an explosion causes a [[stampede]] at a high school in [[Bangui]], [[Central African Republic]]. President [[Faustin-Archange Touadéra]] declares three [[national day of mourning|days of national mourning]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crmvjrnkkjvo (BBC News)]
*At least 11 people are killed and 15 others are missing after a [[landslide]] in [[Medellín]] and [[Bello, Antioquia|Bello]], [[Antioquia Department]], [[Colombia]]. [https://apnews.com/article/colombia-landslide-natural-disaster-rains-weather-9bc6e51e2bc9919c7e0a4be08ac4d744 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2024 Armenian protests]]
**[[Government of Armenia|Armenian authorities]] arrest the archbishop [[Bagrat Galstanyan]] of the [[Armenian Apostolic Church]] and accuse him of [[putsch|plotting]] against the government. [https://apnews.com/article/armenia-archbishop-arrest-pashinyan-azerbaijan-7347c25c5df06e868e3f8c630864ff79 (AP)]
*[[2025 Kenyan protests]]
**At least 16 people are killed and over 400 others are injured, including demonstrators, police officers and journalists, when police [[Mass shooting|clash with]] protestors during nationwide anti-government protests across [[Kenya]]. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/article/eight-deaths-reported-over-400-injured-in-kenya-protests/ (CTV News)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian president]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] and the [[Council of Europe]]'s [[European Commission of Human Rights|Human Rights Office]] sign an accord to establish a [[Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine|special tribunal for crimes in Ukraine]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20250625-zelensky-council-of-europe-rights-body-sign-accord-ukraine-war-tribunal-russia (France 24)]
*[[Anti–money laundering#United States|Anti–money laundering § United States]], [[War on drugs#Mexico|War on drugs § Mexico]]
**[[List of banks in Mexico|Mexican banks]] CIBanco, Intercam Banco, and Vector Casa de Bolsa—the latter owned by [[Alfonso Romo]], former Chief of Staff to President [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]]—are sanctioned by the United States government over alleged [[money laundering]] for [[Mexican drug cartels|drug cartels]]. Mexican president [[Claudia Sheinbaum]] requests that the U.S. government provide evidence. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/money/companies/us-treasury-sanctions-three-mexican-financial-institutions-over-money-laundering-ties/ar-AA1HqEp5 (MSN)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/6/25/us-sanctions-mexican-banks-alleging-connections-to-cartel-money-laundering (Al Jazeera)] [https://forbes.com.mx/sheinbaum-exige-a-eu-que-presente-pruebas-tras-acusaciones-a-ci-banco-intercam-y-vector/ (''Forbes'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2025 NBA Draft]]
**In [[basketball]], the [[NBA draft|NBA Draft]] is held at the [[Barclays Center]] in [[New York City]], [[U.S.]], with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] selecting [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] player [[Cooper Flagg]] as the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]].
